reference.method: damped Newton at 50 digits on the README log density, from the fitted values

global.statement: With both coefficients free, every nonempty count sample has an attained maximum. It is unique if a positive count occurs, including $\lambda=0$ when all positive counts are one. All-zero data give $p_0=1$ and leave the rate unidentified. Holding either coefficient preserves attainment for compatible data. A free zero probability is uniquely the empirical zero fraction. A free rate is unique when positives occur and is unidentified otherwise. Holding all coefficients leaves likelihood evaluation. Held $p_0=0$ excludes zeros, held $p_0=1$ excludes positives, and held $\lambda=0$ permits positive counts only at one.
global.reason: The likelihood factors into a Bernoulli likelihood for the zero indicator and a zero-truncated Poisson likelihood for the positives. The first has its unique maximum at the empirical zero fraction. In the second, the conditional mean $\lambda/(1-e^{-\lambda})$ increases strictly from one to infinity: its derivative with respect to log rate is the positive conditional variance. Therefore the positive sample mean determines a unique rate, with the continuous endpoint $\lambda=0$ for mean one. Without positives the rate drops out of the likelihood.
